extracted.intended_audience: untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professors at U.S. academic institutions and full-time employees at DOE National Laboratories or Office of Science User Facilities seeking DOE Early Career Research Program awards
extracted.subtask_short: DOE Office of Science early career application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the U.S. DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program, including applicant eligibility, program office selection, mandatory pre-application and full-application deadlines, award sizes, and selection basis. Targets early-career researchers at U.S. academic institutions, DOE national labs, and Office of Science user facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility: position and employment
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the program, a researcher must be an untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution or a full-time employee at a DOE National Laboratory or Office of Science User Facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in one of the specified appointment types; the program is targeted to early-career researchers based at U.S. institutions or DOE facilities. The page does not state exceptions or alternative appointment categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility: time-since-doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants must be within 10 years of having earned a doctorate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 10-year limit is an explicit eligibility cutoff. The announcement does not detail allowable extensions (e.g., for family or medical leave) on this page—applicants should consult the program announcement for waiver/extension policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional award destination and approximate award amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to an institution of higher education will be approximately $875,000 over five years and awards to a DOE National Laboratory or Office of Science User Facility will be approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award amounts and durations are approximate totals over five years and differ by host institution type. Applicants should plan budgets consistent with the host-type award level and verify details in the funding opportunity announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program office choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers may apply to one of seven Office of Science program offices: Advanced Scientific Computing Research; Biological and Environmental Research; Basic Energy Sciences; Fusion Energy Sciences; High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics; and Isotope R&D and Production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must select the single Office of Science program office most appropriate for their proposed research. Ensure the chosen office aligns with the project's technical scope and program priorities described in the program announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic fit: topic must fall within Office of Science priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE’s Office of Science, which are provided in the program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear demonstration of how the proposed work maps to the stated programmatic priorities is required; proposals outside those priorities are ineligible. Consult the program announcement for the detailed list of priorities and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pre-application and full-application gatekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are mandatory and are due on March 24, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET. Only those applicants whose pre-application is encouraged by DOE may submit full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission is a two-step process: a required pre-application that is screened, and invitation-only full applications. Failure to submit a timely pre-application or not receiving encouragement precludes submission of a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be due on June 2, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the stated full-application deadline if invited after pre-application review. Verify time zone and submission system requirements in the funding opportunity materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection method: competitive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding will be competitively awarded on the basis of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be evaluated by peer reviewers—expect evaluation against scientific merit, programmatic relevance, and other standard peer-review criteria detailed in the program announcement. Prepare materials to address likely review criteria (significance, approach, investigators, innovation, environment, etc.), as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal: stimulate new research directions in mission-critical areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will advance ... providing five-year awards to exceptional early career researchers ... to stimulate new research directions in mission critical areas supported by DOE’s Office of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should emphasize novel directions, potential for high impact in mission-critical DOE science areas, and how the award will enable new lines of inquiry. Aligning with the program's mission-driven objectives strengthens competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding availability and congressional appropriations contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Total planned funding is up to $145 million, with $79 million in Fiscal Year 2026 dollars and outyear funding contingent on congressional appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award availability for future years depends on appropriations; program scale and number of awards may vary. Applicants should be aware that outyear funding is subject to federal budget processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference materials: program announcement and past award abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The programmatic priorities are provided in the program announcement. Fiscal Year 2010–2025 award abstracts are available on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the full program announcement for detailed eligibility rules, review criteria, application instructions, allowable costs, and any waiver/extension policies. Reviewing past award abstracts can help position proposals and understand prior funded topics and scope.
